text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- An editorial says the attack by republican guardsmen at Tirana's military hospital on Sunday shows that President Sali Berisha wants to trigger conflicts among state institutions.
- Hands off the white uniform, cried out some 600 hospital workers in Tirana after 50-60 guardsmen stormed the hospital and terrorised staff.

- Achille Ochetto, head of the Italian parliament's foreign affairs commission said the Italian government should replace its ambassador in Albania Paolo Foresti and launch investigations over media allegations that Foresti had backed Berisha's Democratic Party.
- Gramshi residents opened fire and threw bombs when King Leka visited their town to seek support for a restoration of the monarchy, the paper says. No casualties were reported.
- Paper publishes document showing that former central bank governor Kristaq Luniku had warned about the risks of pyramid investment schemes from April last year.
ALBANIA
- A survey by the Social Research Institute shows that rightist parties will win over 50 percent of the seats in the next parliament.
- Fights between rival gangs in the southern town of Berat have brought the town to a standstill.
- The Democratic Party's secretary-general Genc Pollo called on all political forces to sign a social pact in order to avoid tension and violence during the electoral campaign.
- An editorial accuses the Socialists of allegedly backing gangs in the south, saying they should be isolated together with the criminals who keep Albania hostage.
- Albanian socialism represents nothing other than rebellion and dictatorship, President Sali Berisha told a crowd in the port town of Durres.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Socialist leader Fatos Nano said general elections might be postponed because the Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe did not understand concerns over joint action monitoring.
- Opposition parties want the state of emergency and curfew to be lifted, new heads of the secret police appointed.
- OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky and Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini have asked Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino to dissolve salvation committees in the south.

- Vranitzky said the OSCE cannot provide electoral guarantees but would provide support and aid. He added they could not protect all voting centres with the 6,000 soldiers of a multinational force in Albania.
- President Berisha has decreed the Central Election Commission made up by representatives from ten parties.
- Calm has returned to the southern city of Kucove after two rival bands fought for half a day. Two people were killed and several wounded.
- Sidorela Kola, a former Miss Albania, has declined to forgive the Klan weekly magazine and a photographer for printing her topless picture without permission.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The international community has urged Albania's leftist parties to participate in upcoming elections.
- Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu is visiting Italy on the invitation of Italian rightist parties.
- Paper blames doctors in Tirana military hospital for not saving a guardsman wounded during gunfight in Cerrik.
